title: Sumo Wrestling with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js sumo wrestling game featuring particle effects. Load the 'flamingo.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN (use https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js).

## Scene Setup
- Create a circular sumo ring (dohyo) as a cylinder with radius 5, height 0.3, colored sandy brown (#DEB887), centered at y=0.15. Add a white torus ring on top at the edge (radius 4.8, tube 0.08) to mark the boundary.
- Floor plane beneath the ring, dark gray.
- Camera: perspective at position (0, 8, 12), looking at origin.
- Lights: ambient (intensity 0.5) + directional from (5, 10, 5) with shadows enabled.
- Skybox or background color: dark navy (#1a1a2e).

## Fighters
- **Player fighter (P1):** Load flamingo.glb, scale to (0.02, 0.02, 0.02), tint/color it RED by traversing the mesh and setting material color to red (#ff3333). Place at (0, 0.3, 3). This is controlled by the player.
- **AI fighter (P2):** Load a second instance of flamingo.glb, scale to (0.02, 0.02, 0.02), tint BLUE (#3333ff). Place at (0, 0.3, -3). This is AI controlled.
- Each fighter has properties: position, velocity, mass=1, health=100, pushForce=0.
- Play any animation found in the GLB file for both fighters (loop it).

## Physics & Movement
- Player controls P1 with WASD keys: W=forward(-Z), S=back(+Z), A=left(-X), D=right(+X). Movement speed: 0.08 per frame.
- Pressing SPACE performs a 'push attack' — applies a force impulse toward the opponent if distance < 2.5 units. The push reduces opponent health by 10 and pushes them back by 1.5 units in the direction away from attacker. Add a 500ms cooldown on attacks.
- AI moves toward the player at speed 0.04 per frame and attacks when within range 2.5 (also with 500ms cooldown).
- Friction: multiply velocities by 0.92 each frame.
- Ring-out detection: if a fighter's XZ distance from center > 5.0, they lose immediately (health set to 0).

## Particle Effects
- On each push attack hit, spawn 20 particles at the collision point. Particles are small spheres (radius 0.05) colored orange-yellow, with random velocities. They fade out over 0.8 seconds and are removed.
- When a fighter is eliminated (health<=0 or ring-out), spawn 50 larger particles (radius 0.1) in the loser's color that burst outward.
- Maintain a particle array and update positions each frame.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left: P1 health bar (red, 200px wide div, height shrinks proportionally).
- Top-right: P2 health bar (blue, 200px wide div).
- Center top: Round counter text 'Round X' (start at Round 1).
- A 'Start Game' button centered on screen. Game begins paused; clicking this starts the match. Hide button on click.
- When a fighter wins, show 'Player Wins!' or 'AI Wins!' message centered, and a 'Next Round' button. Clicking it resets positions, restores health to 100, increments round counter, and starts again.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- gameStarted: boolean (false initially, true after Start clicked)
- roundNumber: number (starts 1)
- p1Health: number (0-100)
- p2Health: number (0-100)
- p1Position: {x, y, z} — current position of player fighter
- p2Position: {x, y, z} — current position of AI fighter
- p1Attacking: boolean — true during attack cooldown
- p2Attacking: boolean
- activeParticles: number — count of currently active particles in scene
- matchOver: boolean — true when a fighter is eliminated
- winner: string — 'player' or 'ai' or 'none'
- ringRadius: 5.0 (constant)
- distanceBetweenFighters: number — live Euclidean XZ distance

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Fighters must stay on the ring surface (y~0.3). Velocity damping factor 0.92/frame. Push attack applies 1.5 unit knockback. Ring-out at XZ distance > 5.0 from center. Attack cooldown 500ms. Health decrements by 10 per hit. No NaN in positions or velocities.
